title: Consider Doing It in Reverse
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Opening with the fitness trend of walking backward, the post argues that reversing the usual direction of thinking can yield useful insight in leadership. It applies reverse thinking to three areas: planning a long-term goal from its end point, planning a career from the desired final roles, and developing skills by working backward through the sub-skills with the help of an expert. It then singles out reviewing a decision in reverse, from outcome back through sub-decisions, as the most powerful use because it isolates what really drove the result. The author concludes that few people operate this way, which gives those who do an edge.
points: Working backward from an end point clarifies the steps a team must take toward a long-term goal.
Career planning gains clarity when the final roles and accomplishments are chosen first.
Asking an expert to walk backward through a skill reveals the critical sub-skills and their order.
Reviewing a good decision in reverse shows which sub-decisions to replicate.
quotes: Many leaders employ a reverse approach when planning to achieve a long-term goal. Thinking strategically from the end point and working backward, identifying the steps the team needs to take to accomplish the goal, can prove highly insightful.

The same is true with career planning. Deciding the end goals of a career — the roles and accomplishments one desires to achieve before hanging up the cleats — and then working backward to identify the skills and positions one needs to get there can create much-needed clarity.

Operating in reverse also benefits skill development. Of course, it’s essential to know the actions and practices needed to advance any skill. Someone who already possesses the skill will know what order of sub-skills must be mastered. Engaging such an expert in looking backward can be a real eye-opener.

Of the many reverse approaches to improvement and planning that aid effectiveness, perhaps none is more powerful than reviewing what went right and wrong along the way to a quality decision. Starting from the outcome of the decision and reviewing the sub-decisions in reverse provides a laser-like focus on what really contributed to the end result.
Reverse thinking and reverse doing are worth considering in nearly every process and desired outcome. The clarity provided can be a game-changer.
